query: What kinds of hardware issues appear in these incidents?

per_column.name: hardware_component_type
per_column.rationale: The affected hardware component (printer, server, monitor, etc.) is a constitutive 'what part' aspect of a hardware issue -- a genuine part-of decomposition of what the hiccup concerns.

per_column.name: hardware_failure_mode
per_column.rationale: The failure mode (connectivity issue, not working, overheating, physical damage) is the 'how it fails' aspect, an intrinsic dimension of the hardware issue itself.

per_column.name: device_location_scope
per_column.rationale: The spatial/organizational scope of the affected device (individual workstation vs network-wide vs building infrastructure) is an aspect OF the incident's hardware footprint -- a plausible facet characterizing the hiccup.

per_column.name: resolution_category
per_column.rationale: Resolution category describes the remediation/handling of the issue, not a constitutive aspect of the hardware hiccup itself. The fix is downstream of and external to the concept being decomposed.

per_column.name: is_peripheral_device
per_column.rationale: This boolean is a coarse re-derivation of hardware_component_type (peripheral/keyboard/printer vs server/network). It restates information already captured by the component-type facet rather than adding a distinct aspect.

judge.rationale: Three columns (component_type, failure_mode, location_scope) are genuine constitutive facets carving the hardware-hiccup concept into what/how/where aspects, giving reasonable exhaustiveness of its main constitutive dimensions. However, mutual exclusivity is weakened: is_peripheral_device overlaps heavily with hardware_component_type, and resolution_category is an external remediation attribute rather than a facet of the concept. Removing the two non-facet columns would yield a cleaner MECE decomposition.
